 SubjectiveAssociated Press — Senate, every stateThe Senate file in its latest state: 35 races listed, Alaska and Mississippi both too early to call, and the remaining races called state by state.

 SubjectivePoliwave — the House live results fileUpdated November 6 at 1:28 p.m. EST: 254 House seats called for the Democrats and 164 for the Republicans, with eight more led by the Democrats and nine by the Republicans, 418 of 435 races called.

 SubjectiveBeeBulletin, carrying NBC News — the midterm results so farUpdated November 6: NBC News has called 250 House seats for the Democrats and 161 for the Republicans, with 24 uncalled, and estimates a final 259 to 176 if the leads hold; the Senate stands called at 54 to 44; and tallies are stated to differ between outlets and to change as races are called.

 SubjectiveDaily Caller — both parties raise recount funds as the counting persistsDays after the polls closed, both Senate campaign committees have created recount funds; the Associated Press figures of early Friday afternoon put Colom ahead by about 2,000 votes at 49.1 percent to 48.8 percent in Mississippi, with more than 95 percent counted, and Peltola ahead at 48.17 percent to 47.8 percent in Alaska with 74 percent counted; the Republican committee’s letter demanding affidavit ballots be separated and preserved; and the Sullivan campaign’s statement that a ranked-choice tabulation run today would put Sullivan ahead 105,037 to 104,709.

 SubjectiveThe Rico TV — a new ballot return shifts the Mississippi Senate raceColom’s lead pushed to 1,936 votes on Friday morning after returns from Bolivar County gave him a net gain of 123, and to 2,010 in a subsequent state report; the contest remained uncalled with absentee and affidavit ballots still being processed; mailed ballots postmarked by Election Day must arrive by November 10 and counties certify by November 13; and Alaska’s tally is recorded unchanged, with its next major update expected Tuesday.

 SubjectiveThe Coloradoan — when the 4th District result will be seenUpdated at about 2 p.m. on November 6: Boebert trails Laubacher by 3,278 votes, 48.78 percent to 47.92, with the Libertarian at 3.31 percent; at least 5,000 ballots remain in the four most populous counties by the account’s estimate; 474 district ballots await signature cure; and an automatic recount would be triggered at about 926 votes.

 SubjectiveAmerican Muckrakers — the 4th District update: the lead grows to 3,069The wire’s Friday-midday totals: Laubacher 184,624, Boebert 181,555, the Libertarian 12,506, a lead of 3,069 on 378,685 counted; the state’s Thursday-night figures at 3,024; the Boebert campaign lawyer’s statement that the campaign is investigating unusual voting patterns; the cure and military deadline of November 12; and a projection of a final margin near 3,900, in a stated range of 2,800 to 4,600.

 SubjectiveChristianity Now — Johnson steps aside, Jordan and Scalise seek the postWashington, November 5: House Republicans choose a new leader on November 10 after Speaker Johnson decided against seeking the minority leader post; candidates had until noon on November 6 to declare; Jordan’s and Scalise’s letters to colleagues are recorded; Jeffries has formally launched his bid for speaker; and the lame-duck funding measure past December is named as the business ahead.

 SubjectiveWikipedia — the 2026 House Republican Conference leadership electionThe election’s record: the conference votes November 10, 2026, before the 120th Congress; representatives had until November 6 to declare; Scalise and Jordan are the declared candidates for minority leader, with their districts and present posts; Speaker Johnson has ruled out a run; and one incumbent committee chair’s re-election had yet to be called as of November 6.

 SubjectiveSignal Post News — the Iran war decision: “Maybe I’ll have to”Washington, November 6: the president, after his first post-midterm national security meeting, said he will soon decide whether to resume all-out war, laid out the choice as going further until the nuclear program can be certified dead or stopping short of destroying the rest of the country, and said no new strikes have been ordered and no decision announced; Central Command is finalizing preparations without a new directive; and the Theodore Roosevelt group’s Singapore stop and mid-November arrival are recorded.

 SubjectiveGlobalSecurity.org — the Iran war, day 252 update, November 6The operations file with a 0500 ET cutoff: the president weighing resumed operations and Central Command finalizing preparations without a directive; officials noting November 9 is a new moon; Iran’s formal nuclear proposal sent through Qatar, with its seven demands including compensation, an end to sanctions and the blockade, release of frozen assets, and a permanent end to the war; Rapidan’s Bob McNally putting the chance of fighting resuming at 80 percent; and 18 Americans stated killed in total.

 SubjectiveSilent Dossier — why the Kremlin says it has no details on the dealNovember 6: spokesman Peskov’s answer in three words, there are no details; Dmitriev has not yet returned from the United States or reported to President Putin; no European ideas on security guarantees have reached Russia; the White House event marking the Oleshky ceasefire is described; and delegations from Washington, Moscow, and Kyiv are due in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11.

 SubjectiveAssociated Press, via Military.com — Zelenskyy presses allies for clear postwar guaranteesKyiv: President Zelenskyy seeks specific guarantees, clear on paper, on what happens if Russia attacks again—who will do what, with what means, and when; the comments followed two days of Brussels talks on postwar security, reconstruction, and 2027 funding; lead negotiator Umerov’s post on the threats discussed is quoted; and Zelenskyy said Ukraine’s chances of additional American assistance may now grow.

 Subjectivebne IntelliNews, via EuropeSays — the United States offers European security talks but no vetoNo country would hold a veto over another’s alliances in a new framework, envoy Kushner said on November 5, listing five goals including permanent consultations, crisis communications, military transparency, and reciprocal de-escalation measures; Peskov’s November 3 statement that guarantees can only be mutual is carried; the Abu Dhabi meeting is put at working level on November 10–11 with Medinsky leading Russia’s team; and European leaders meet in Berlin on November 19.
